thread:
maria (Support): Hey team, customer reported intermittent 502s + big latency spikes yesterday afternoon for their account (acct_845). They also say billing shows an itemized token surge that doesn't match their traffic. Trace/req ids attached: trace=tr-0a9f3, req=1785123456-01, req=1785123456-02. Can we collect repro steps and a debug snapshot? :eyes:

ops-bot: Automated notice: deployment(redwood-v2.1-canary) rolled at 2024-11-07T15:24:10Z to us-east-1. No cluster-wide alerts at deploy time.

zach (Eng-ML): Thanks Maria. Quick triage questions: 1) Are the failing requests hitting the canary or the stable model? 2) Do we have KV-cache hits logged for those req ids? 3) Any auth failures in the same window?

maria (Support): From customer-provided curl they hit model=redwood-v2 (no explicit version tag). Logs show a fallback to redwood-v1-small for some reqs (see req=1785123456-02). No auth failures. KV-cache shows mixed hit/miss pattern for that session.

aaron (Customer): I can reproduce consistently when sending a specific prompt (short system + ~800 token user). Happens in ~30% of tries. Curl I ran: 

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v2","input":"<customer prompt here>","max_tokens":512}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

Response: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
{"error":"upstream timeout","request_id":"1785123456-02","duration_ms":12048}

maria (Support): Aaron also attached a HAR and the exact timestamp for a failure: 2024-11-07T16:03:12Z. He noted cost spike on 11/07 between 16:00-16:30 UTC.

eli (Billing): I pulled billing events: there are multiple small attribution entries for reconciling model variants. Looks like some requests were billed at 'v2.1-canary' rates and some at 'v1-small' rates. We need the request_ids to map usages to model variants — Maria you already listed two, can you get the full list?

sasha (Prod Eng): Plan of action: a) collect full server-side logs + inference engine traces for req ids (trace, kv hits, kernel selection) b) get a debug bundle from the customer's tenant (we have a helper endpoint) c) reproduce locally with pinned model version to compare behavior (stable vs canary) d) if repro is consistent, run a targeted rollout rollback for that tenant. I can own the rollback if we confirm.

zach (Eng-ML): For (b) debug bundle steps for the customer: run our internal helper (support) to snapshot logs. Maria please ask Aaron to run the signed one-time URL I generated: https://internal.redwood/snapshot?token=snap-7cde (expires 1h). It will gather request traces, kernel selection logs, and kv-cache heatmap. Share that bundle here when done.

maria (Support): Sent the snap link to Aaron. Also asked him to run the curl with --trace-ascii and attach the output.

aaron (Customer): Uploaded the trace file and HAR to the shared support artifact. One more datapoint: when I add "?model=redwood-v1-small" explicitly the calls succeed but latency is higher (~900ms) and charges are lower. So it seems fallback avoids 502s but the customer needs v2 quality.

sasha (Prod Eng): That's interesting — fallback reduces failure rate but hard regresses latency/quality. Could be a KV cache invalidation causing a hot-path to trigger slow kernel selection or an OOM leading to upstream timeout. Zach, can you check mem spikes in the infer runtime around trace tr-0a9f3?

zach (Eng-ML): On it. I spun up the inference lane logs for that window. Preliminary: we see a sequence length jump (customer prompt + system ~1200 tokens) causing unexpected attention allocation; kernel chooser picked slower fallback kernel on a subset of shards. Also observed one node reporting a transient 12s stall which matches the 12048ms duration in Aaron's curl.

infra-bot: Alert: node gpu-19 reported high_grad_mem at 2024-11-07T16:02:59Z, pid=4123, evicted_kv_segments=2.

maria (Support): Good catch. Customer's prompt is near the upper bounds. Next steps we've agreed: 1) collect full debug bundle (Aaron uploaded, link attached in thread) 2) Zach to extract kernel selection + mem traces and share short summary 3) Sasha to run a targeted repro in canary vs stable pinned versions (instructions below) 4) If repro confirmed, schedule a tenant-specific pin to stable and rollback canary for that tenant, then coordinate billing correction if needed.

zach (Eng-ML): Summary to paste in ticket: kernel chooser flipped to 'block-attn-v1' on 3/8 shards at request start due to long seq length; mid-request eviction of two KV segments triggered re-compile path that caused stall and upstream timeout. Proposed mitigation: add a conservative pre-flight check that forces either 1) larger kv-reservation or 2) immediate fallthrough to stable kernel for seq>1000 on canary. I'll draft a short patch.

sasha (Prod Eng): For repro steps (pin matrix):
1) Pin model query param to redwood-v2@2024-09-21 (stable sha) and run 50 sequential requests using Aaron's prompt.
2) Pin to redwood-v2.1-canary and run same 50 requests.
3) Collect success rate, p95 latency, and kernel selection logs; attach qsub ids.

maria (Support): I'm creating a customer ticket with the plan and ETA. Aaron — can you confirm you'll keep running tests when we ask? We may ask you to re-run after we push a hotfix.

aaron (Customer): Yes, I can run tests on request. Appreciate the quick scope and plan.

eli (Billing): Once we confirm pin/rollback, I can run a billing reconciliation to correct any misattributed charges for that 30-min window. Hold off on refunds until we have root cause and patch.

sasha (Prod Eng): Assignments: Zach -> root cause & patch PR, Sasha -> roll/pin for tenant + canary rollback if needed, Maria -> coordinate with customer + collect bundles, Eli -> billing reconciliation. Aim to have reproducible results within 4 hours.

maria (Support): Noted. Adding ticket number SUP-2024-9923 and will update with debug bundle link and cURL traces. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
